metadata.topic: Gas Laws — Boyle's Law: New Volume at Higher Pressure
metadata.note: Follows Q3c(ii) graph-reading (not auto-gradeable). V₁ ≈ 53.3 cm³ at P₁ = 250 kPa is derived from graph (gradient = 13 333 kPa⋅cm³ at point 0.030, 400). Wide tolerance accommodates 'own figure' marking where students used different V₁ readings.

question.name: CSEC Phy May 2022 Q3c(iii) — Boyle's Law: Volume at 975 kPa
question.text:
From the graph in Q3c(ii), the volume of the gas at a pressure of 250 kPa is approximately 53.3 cm³.

Using Boyle's Law, calculate the new volume of the gas when the pressure is increased from 250 kPa to 975 kPa (temperature constant). (4 marks)
question.general_feedback:
Model solution (using graph-read V₁ = 53.3 cm³):
Boyle's Law: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂ (constant temperature)
P₁V₁ = 250 × 53.3 = 13 325 kPa⋅cm³
V₂ = P₁V₁ / P₂ = 13 325 / 975 = 13.7 cm³

Own figure marking: CSEC awards full marks if Boyle's law is correctly applied to whatever V₁ the student read from the graph.

steps.label:
Given: P₁ = 250 kPa, V₁ = 53.3 cm³ (from graph)  |  P₂ = 975 kPa
Boyle's Law: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂ (at constant temperature)
Calculate P₁ × V₁ and find V₂. (4 marks)

error_codes.SC_CALCULATION_ERROR: P₁ × V₁ = 250 × 53.3 = 13 325. Multiply initial pressure by initial volume.

error_codes.SC_FORMULA_SELECTION_ERROR: Boyle's Law: P₁V₁ = P₂V₂ → V₂ = P₁V₁/P₂. Divide the product P₁V₁ by P₂ = 975 kPa.
